content.title: About
content.content: Margarita is a classic cocktail made of tequila, lime juice, and orange liqueur (triple sec or Cointreau). It is served in a glass with a salt‑rimmed edge and often garnished with a lime wedge. The drink originated in Mexico in the mid‑20th century and quickly gained worldwide popularity.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recorded Margarita recipe dates back to the 1930s in Tijuana, Mexico.
There are many variations, including fruit‑puree versions, berry twists, or swapping tequila for rum (known as a "Tommy Jerry").
The traditional salt rim can be replaced with sugar, spices, or a salt‑and‑chili mix for extra heat.
Margarita is often considered a celebratory drink and is served at parties, weddings, and bars worldwide.
In the United States during the 1970s, Margarita became the best‑selling cocktail in restaurants.

items.title: Vitamin C from lime
items.content: Lime juice is rich in vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Beneficial plant compounds
items.content: Tequila, derived from agave, contains small amounts of polyphenols that may have anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Moderate consumption may promote relaxation
items.content: Alcohol in moderate amounts can help reduce stress and improve mood.

items.title: Alcohol content
items.content: Margarita contains alcohol, so it should be consumed responsibly, avoided before driving, and is not recommended for pregnant individuals or those with liver disease.

items.title: Salt rim
items.content: The salted rim adds sodium, which may be undesirable for people with hypertension.

items.title: Lime acidity
items.content: The acidity can irritate sensitive stomachs and cause heartburn.

items.title: Allergies to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to tequila (agave) or to orange liqueur.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Serve Margarita in a salt‑rimmed glass, garnish with a lime wedge. For a frozen version, blend the ingredients with ice until smooth. To lighten the drink, reduce the amount of tequila and increase lime juice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Alcoholic components (tequila, liqueur) should be kept in tightly sealed bottles in a cool, dark place. Fresh lime juice is best used immediately, but can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 days.
